I guess I only mention it because I hate MMO's where it feels like the DPS just sit and do damage and never have any other effect on the success or failure of the fights. I don't feel like this game suffers from that problem, and always feel like I'm contributing in a meaningful, functional way as a DPS, aside from just pumping big numbers into the boss.

caveat: I just recently returned to the game after about a 6 month break, so I missed some content and am catching back up. If any information below is inaccurate please tell me and I will edit.

First, let's talk queue times. The game uses 4 / 8 player frameworks for dungeons. This means there's always going to be a bit more demand for tanks / healers, simply because there has to be one of them for every 2 DPS that queue. This kind of means that SE is banking on the idea that there will be 2 dps players for every player queueing as a tank or healer, so for everyone to have instant queues we'd need 50% of the playerbase to be playing DPS classes, and 25% tanks and 25% heals.

This actually works out pretty well. DPS queues are NOT that much longer than tank / healer queues, and I think we have the 4 / 8 system to thank for that.

I say all this to illustrate that it's a mistake to pick your job based on queue times. If you want to dps, do so. It won't slow you down all that much in terms of finding dungeons.

Second, not all jobs are created equal and all have unique playstyles and advantages / disadvantages.

Bard is fun and arguably one of the easiest classes to play well, but you have the healer limit break -This is no longer true. Bards have a DPS limit break now, thanks /u/Fiery1ce and a lot of support abilities that allow you to really help the group in tight situations, which can be a huge game changer if done correctly. I think the hardest thing I've ever really had to do as a bard is kite things (rarely) or participate in interrupt rotations, which isn't all that challenging either. You can run and cast all of your abilities on the move unlike...

Black Mage's have to cast so high movement fights (90% of end-game battles are high movement in this game imo) are challenging but fun. I'm not a 50 blm so that's about all the insight I can offer. You have an AOE limit break that does damage in a large area, and is very useful in some fights.

Summoner is another casting class that's DOT and pet based damage. You will summon little companions that are based on the primals that deal damage and bring utilities to the party. Summoners are doing a lot of damage right now from what I understand, and they can also cross-class instant resurrections and a have a few other utility spells that make them a good addition to any group.

Monk, Dragoon, & Ninja are the 3 flavors of melee dps available. They each bring small unique things to the group (ninja's can renew a friendly party member's TP, Dragoons can debuff enemies, ect) but for the most part the melee experience is pretty similar between the three. Fun rotations and a lot more footwork to deal with in terms of making some attacks on certain sides of an enemy, and dodging various melee abilities. Melee is harder than ranged dps IMO but very rewarding.

White Mage, Scholar are the two healing classes available at level 1. They fill the same role but do it in different ways. WHM is more direct heals and hots, where as Scholar has a pet helping to heal, and they have shielding and buffs built into their healing that make them slightly less direct. If you've played WoW, I think it's a reasonably accurate comparison to think of WHM as a holy priest and Scholar as a discipline priest. They both bring unique things to the table and most groups want one of each.

Warrior and Gladiator are the two tank classes. Warriors are (were? Been a while since I tanked, the info here may be outdated) are perceived to do more damage, and if they don't jump into defiance stance (ability that lowers their DPS and increases their enmity and survivability) they can do almost as much as a full-fledged DPS. Gladiators were better at absorbing damage back when I was tanking, but either class is an absolutely viable option to tank, and it kind of comes down to playstyle and preference. You want a sword and shield, or a big ol' axe?

Dark Knight, Astrologian, & Machinist all start at level 30. Dark Knight is a tank somewhere between WAR and GLD, Astrologian is a healer somewhere between WHM and SCH, and Machinist is a lot like Bard. Don't know much about them, or if it's even possible to switch to them right when you get one of your other jobs to 30? Anybody else that can answer that?

FINAL POINT There isn't really a shortage of anything. There seems to be players on all jobs, and as someone mentioned already, you can be max level in multiple jobs, so most people have a handful they can play and adjust to make a cohesive group to face content. (personally I play WHM > BRD > WAR) Join an FC and start leveling the one you LIKE, not the one you think they need. By the time you max out they probably won't need what they said they did when you started anyway. (happened to me, I leveled bard and when I got to max my FC had 3 bards and I had to start leveling WHM... haha)

Bards got a stance in HW that increases damage but gives all abilities a cast timer (IE: You have to be stationary to use them). They also can't use their new HW abilities without being in that stance. You description is great for the first 50 levels, but HW added some extra nuance.

The same is true for SMN, previously touted as the far more mobile spellcaster compared to BLM. They are still incredibly mobile by comparison, make no mistake, but the dreadwyrm trance mechanic (namely, ruin 3) makes turretting up a DPS gain.

Lastly, the difference between White Mage and Scholar has become less pronounced at level 60, especially compared to early 2.0. This is generally a good thing, but the main difference now comes in style. Scholars tend to mitigate damage and thus benefit from a better understanding of fight mechanics (being able to predict damage), where white mages heal by raw numbers and don't have many preventative measures available.

FFXIV is actually great at breaking people into new roles that they're unfamiliar with. Where other MMOs would have you level solo and then just expect you to know exactly what you're doing in a group, this game has these things called "guildhests" that are basically little group challenges specifically designed to teach you how to react to certain mechanics. Stuff on the ground you shouldn't stand in, how to deal with adds, how to focus on a certain mob that should be killed first, etc. I've found it to be super helpful. Give it a try, you might like it!
